# STM32H743 FC + 80A 4-in-1 ESC: Power-Stage Loss Model, Thermal Model, Bi-Directional DShot600 Timer/DMA Allocation, and Reference Netlist

## 0. Scope and Architectural Assumptions

I have no prior "Job #3" specification, so every number below comes from a stated assumption. Replace the values in Table 0 with your BOM datasheet values. All equations are written so the numbers can simply be swapped in.

**Architectural correction.** The 48 kHz PWM is not generated by the STM32H743. A 4-in-1 ESC carries its own MCU per channel or a shared one, typically an STM32G071 or AT32F421 running AM32 or BLHeli_32. The H743 flight controller runs ArduPilot and talks to the ESC over bi-directional DShot600. The document is therefore split into three domains:

| Domain | Silicon | Concern |
|---|---|---|
| Flight controller | STM32H743 @ 400 MHz | DShot600 generation, eRPM capture, DMA |
| ESC logic | e.g. STM32G071 (×1 or ×4) | 48 kHz 6-step/FOC PWM, dead time |
| ESC power stage | 24× N-MOSFET + 3-phase gate drivers | Conduction, switching and thermal losses |

**Table 0 – Baseline assumptions**

| Symbol | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| V_bus | 25.2 V | 6S fully charged, worst case for switching loss |
| I_burst | 80 A | Per-channel phase current, burst |
| t_burst | 2 s (also evaluated at 0.5 s and 5 s) | Burst duration |
| f_sw | 48 kHz | ESC PWM frequency |
| R_ds(on),25 | 1.0 mΩ | Per MOSFET at V_GS = 10 V. One FET per switch position (6 per channel) |
| α_R | 0.0045 /K | R_ds(on) temperature coefficient (≈1.45× at 125 °C) |
| t_r, t_f | 20 ns, 15 ns | Effective V-I overlap times with the chosen gate resistor |
| t_dt | 200 ns | Dead time per edge |
| V_SD | 0.8 V | Body-diode forward voltage at 80 A, hot |
| Q_rr | 40 nC | Body-diode reverse-recovery charge |
| C_oss,eff | 1.0 nF | Energy-related output capacitance at 25 V |
| Q_g | 50 nC | Total gate charge at 10 V |
| R_θJC | 1.2 K/W | Junction to exposed pad (DFN 3.3×3.3 or 5×6) |
| T_amb | 40 °C | Ambient air inside the frame |

## 1. Conduction-Loss Model (80 A Burst)

### 1.1 Current path

With synchronous (complementary) 6-step commutation, two switch positions carry the phase current at every instant:

- the PWM leg, either its high-side FET (on-time) or its low-side FET (synchronous-rectification off-time), and
- the low-side FET of the return leg, which is held on for the full 60° sector.

The current is therefore always flowing through exactly two R_ds(on) elements. Ignoring dead time (handled in §2.3):

$$P_{cond,ch} = I_{ph,rms}^2 \cdot 2 \cdot R_{ds(on)}(T_j)$$

At high throttle the inductor ripple is small compared with 80 A, so I_rms ≈ I_ph. For a ripple correction use:

$$I_{rms}^2 = I_{ph}^2 + \frac{\Delta I_{pp}^2}{12}$$

### 1.2 Temperature dependence and self-consistent solution

R_ds(on) rises with junction temperature, and junction temperature rises with loss:

$$R_{ds}(T_j) = R_{25}\,[1 + \alpha_R (T_j - 25)]$$

$$T_j = T_{ref} + P_{FET}(T_j)\, Z_{\theta}(t)$$

Substituting, with P_FET = k · R_ds(T_j) and k = I² for a FET conducting full-time:

$$T_j = \frac{T_{ref} + k R_{25} Z_\theta (1 - 25\alpha_R)}{1 - k R_{25}\alpha_R Z_\theta}$$

**Thermal runaway condition.** A stable operating point exists only if

$$k R_{25}\alpha_R Z_\theta < 1$$

At 80 A: k·R₂₅·α_R = 6400 × 1e-3 × 0.0045 = 0.0288 W/K. Runaway therefore occurs at Z_θ > 34.7 K/W, which is the hard ceiling on junction-to-reference thermal impedance.

### 1.3 Numbers at T_j ≈ 100 °C

- R_ds = 1.0 × (1 + 0.0045 × 75) = 1.34 mΩ
- P_cond,ch = 80² × 2 × 1.34 mΩ = **17.1 W per channel**
